az_ashlan.description:
He's at the Face itself, deep in Azurelode Mine, south of Southpoint. He carries a mattock with silver worked into the head. It was a waste of good silver, and he knew it, and he had it made anyway.

I've had his job two years. I'd rather not have it this literally, and I'd rather the men stopped asking me whether he'd have called them back.
az_ashlan.accept_text: If the mattock's still in one piece, bring it up. The men will want to see it on the wall.

az_grimewick.description:
Azurelode Mine, south of Southpoint. The pump house is past the sump.

He took a candle down into a gallery full of pump gas, which is how the whole thing started, and the gas is what killed the shift. Thirty years I've blamed the engineers. Turns out it was one kobold and a candle, and he's still holding the candle.
az_grimewick.accept_text: Put that candle out when he's done. I'd hate for him to finish the job thirty years late.

az_kobolds.description:
Go to Azurelode Mine, south of Southpoint, in through the adit in the rock face, and mind the standing water. It's deeper than the light makes it look, and it doesn't drain anywhere.

That should clear the upper galleries. They'll be back, they're always back. I'd settle for walking my own mine without a torch in one hand and an axe in the other.
az_kobolds.accept_text: Light your lamp before you go through the adit. The first gallery bends, and they wait round it.

az_prospectors.description: There are Syndicate men in the flooded galleries, and they're measuring, not digging. They sound the depth, chalk the walls, and run chain along the sump. There's exactly one reason to measure a drowned mine that carefully, and it's to work out what draining it would cost.
az_prospectors.accept_text:
They're below the causeway in Azurelode Mine, south of Southpoint. You'll hear the chain before you see the lamps, because they sound the depth every ten paces and log it.

Alterac sold the pass to the Horde in the Second War, and the Alliance dissolved the kingdom for it. The lords scattered into these hills with nothing. This is what nothing looks like when it finds a silver seam it used to own.
az_prospectors.turn_in_text: They were chalking depths on the wall in a hand I recognise from estate maps. Bandits don't work like that. Somebody up there still thinks of this valley as property.

az_silver.description: There's no sense hauling ore to Tarren Mill when the mine's own furnace sits a full six feet above the waterline and has done all along. I want bars, not baskets, and I'd like to know the person bringing them can tell silver from tin. Cut it off the Face and smelt it, at my furnace or any forge in the valley, I don't care whose. I've had three men bring me tin this season with a straight face. Tin out of a mine called Azurelode is a special sort of insult, and I'd rather not be insulted by you.
az_silver.accept_text: Let the bars cool before you stack them. A warm bar takes a dent, and I'll know.

az_survey.accept_text:
Go to the Silver Face, at the top of the workings. You'll know it, because the rock goes blue-violet the moment a lamp touches it.

What I need is whether the causeway still stands. My chart says there's a spine of dry rock running to the Face. If the chart's right, the seam is reachable and this is a mine again. If it's wrong, it's a lake with a door.
az_survey.turn_in_text:
So it's still standing. Then the chart holds, and the Face can be worked.

Don't tell the Overseer yet. He'll put men down there tomorrow, and I'd like to know what else is down there first.

dg_brannic.description: The outer gate of Dun Garok has a warden, and the warden is the reason it's a gate rather than a doorway. Gatewarden Brannic has held the threshold long enough that the Stormpike stopped posting a second man on it. He's there now, south of the mill, with a bearded axe and a shield scarred in a band at exactly shoulder height, and in fifteen years that axe has only ever swung in one doorway. He won't come out to you, because he's never once come out. I've measured that gate twice, and I'd like to walk through it once before I'm too old to enjoy it.
dg_brannic.accept_text: You'll have to go to him, in the one place he's had fifteen years to practise standing. Don't fight him on his terms if you can help it.

dg_dunmar.description: The riflemen on the south road are trained, and the training has a name. Rifle-Sergeant Dunmar runs the barracks off the muster yard in Dun Garok, and I've worked out that killing riflemen on a road is a tax, while killing the man who makes them is a solution. He's in the barracks, east off the muster yard, and there's a sally port up the east wall that reaches it without going through the inner gate. He sights for the length of that yard and no further, same as his men, because he taught them. Inside that distance he's a man with an empty rifle and a sergeant's temper.
dg_dunmar.accept_text: Close the distance before he's reloaded. That's the whole of my advice.

dg_korrin.description: Behind the vault door in Dun Garok is a crypt, and in the crypt is a thane. Thane Korrin Stonewatch was buried in an iron circlet by dwarves who swore to hold the ridge, and he didn't stay buried, and the garrison above has spent a great many years not discussing the noise. He's in the Crypt of Dun Garok, past the vault, with the Stonewatch Greataxe. The oath was to hold the ridge, and he's technically still holding it. I've never had cause to write a more dwarven sentence in a dispatch.
dg_korrin.accept_text: Leave the circlet on him when it's done. It's the one thing in that crypt that's still his.
dg_korrin.turn_in_text:
The Stormpike won't thank us, and they won't admit it happened.

They'll bury him again, deeper, and the next garrison will be told the noise is the wind. That's how a hold keeps a secret: badly, and for centuries.

dg_morgrin.description: There's a door at the back of the Great Hall that the Stormpike keep shut, and a shrine-keeper standing in front of it who's made it his life's work. Nobody in the garrison will say what's behind it. I've asked three times, and three times I've been told to mind my own business. I've decided their silence is the answer. Get that door open, and we'll find out what they're so careful about.
dg_morgrin.turn_in_text:
So it's open, then.

And now we have to decide whether we want to know. Wanting it open was the easy part.

dg_mountaineers.description:
Go after their mountaineers, inside the outer gate of Dun Garok, south of the mill. I need that muster yard quiet long enough to measure it.

And look at the walls while you're in there. There's no chamfer anywhere, no rubble fill, and every corner is a true corner. They didn't tidy up a cave. They cut a hold out of a mountain, square, on purpose, and I'd admire it more if I weren't trying to get into it.
dg_mountaineers.accept_text: Take a measure of the yard while you're there, if you've got the time. I'll want the length.
dg_mountaineers.turn_in_text:
I've measured it. It's twenty-two paces by sixty, and the gates line up to the inch.

I've surveyed six keeps. This is the only one where I could find no mistake to work with.

dh_perenolde.description:
He's in the Lord's Hall, at the heart of the ring. You've done the work that makes this possible, and I'd rather you knew it. Without the fence's ledger and the magister's postings, I'd have sent you in to kill a squatter.

Alterac sold the Alliance to the Horde, and his father signed it. The Alliance dissolved the kingdom and left the family their titles, because titles cost nothing. This is what fifteen years of carrying a title and no country does to a man.

Durnholde Keep is south-east of Tarren Mill, off the east road. You know the archway.
dh_perenolde.accept_text: Bring me something with his seal on it. The magistrate will want proof, and so will I.
dh_perenolde.turn_in_text:
It's finished now.

The Syndicate won't end. There's always another cousin with a sash. But the man who could pay wizards and buy a valley's thieves is on the floor of a hall his family had no claim to, and the ledger, the postings and the name all go north together.

You walked three roads for this. I'll see every one of them is in the dispatch.

dh_revenants.description:
Find whatever is down there in Durnholde Keep, south-east of the mill. The stair is behind the Lord's Hall.

These were the keep's own garrison, Lordaeron's men, the ones who were here when it fell. They didn't leave. The Syndicate have simply built their camp on top of them and agreed not to go downstairs, which is the most honest thing I know about the Syndicate.
dh_revenants.accept_text: Don't break anything with a crest on it. Somebody might still want to know whose men they were.

dh_sable.description: The kennels on Durnholde Keep's east side are the reason nobody has ever got across the bailey unseen. Houndmaster Sable's hounds learned the work faster than her recruits did, which she says to recruits, in front of the hounds. She's at the kennels, in the east bailey, through the breach. She sets the pack on first and fights second, so kill the handler, and the pack is a dozen dogs with nobody shouting at them, and they'll scatter inside a minute. I've watched it the other way round from the ridge, and it doesn't end until there are no more dogs.
dh_sable.accept_text: Stay downwind on the way in. Those dogs smell a stranger before they hear one.
dh_sable.turn_in_text:
The pack went over the wall and didn't come back. Dogs are sensible.

That's the bailey crossable now, which is two years of my reports made obsolete in an afternoon, and I'm delighted about it.

dh_turnkey.description:
The undercroft of Durnholde Keep, south-east of the mill, past the revenants. Thirty keys on a chain and he swings the lot as one.

He kept the cells. In this keep, in those years, there was one prisoner worth keeping and a boy doesn't hold his own keys. I'm aware that's not a military reason. I'm asking anyway.
dh_turnkey.accept_text: If any of the keys are labelled, bring the chain back. I'd like to know which cell was which.

dh_varth.description: Durnholde Keep's gatehouse has a sergeant-at-arms with a gate-warden's halberd and an alarm bell, and the bell is the problem. I've lost two scouting parties to that keep, and both of them to the same bell. Sergeant-at-Arms Varth is in the gatehouse, south-east of the mill, first thing through the archway. He'll sound the alarm before he fights, because that's his whole function, and he's good at it. If you want to get further into that keep than the bailey, the bell has to stop before the shouting starts.
dh_varth.accept_text: Go through the archway fast and low. He watches the road, not the gate's shadow.
dh_varth.turn_in_text:
It's quiet, then, for the first time in two years, quiet at the gate.

Go further in while it lasts.

dh_yvaine.description: The Syndicate's binders are trained, and training needs a trainer. Magister Yvaine holds the west tower of Durnholde Keep, south-east of Tarren Mill, with a staff of Alterac work that somebody re-cut with less patience than the original maker had. She's the reason a scrap camp in the hills can field wizards at all. Her tower is the west one, off the ring, with one door and no other way out, which cuts both ways. I've had my eye on that tower since I took this command, and I'd like it emptied.
dh_yvaine.accept_text: Bring her staff back if it's whole. I'd like to see what the re-cutting did to it.
